'''Cubic spline interpolation''' finds a piecewise cubic function $C$ that passes through the data points $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=0}^{n}$ and has a continuous second derivative. Continuity of $\ddot{C}$ removes the corner that [[Piecewise linear interpolation|piecewise linear interpolation]] leaves at every knot, and the piecewise form avoids the oscillation of a single interpolating polynomial of high degree ([[Polynomial interpolation]]).<ref>{{#cite:Q2382}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let $x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n$ and let $y_0,\dots,y_n$ be given. The '''knots''' $x_i$ split $[x_0,x_n]$ into $n$ pieces, and on piece $i$ the interpolant is the cubic

$$
C_i(x) = a_i(x-x_i)^3 + b_i(x-x_i)^2 + c_i(x-x_i) + d_i, \qquad i = 0,\dots,n-1,
$$

so that

$$
C(x) = C_i(x), \qquad x_i \le x \le x_{i+1}.
$$

$C$ is a '''cubic spline interpolant''' of the data if

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_i(x_i) &= y_i, && i = 0,\dots,n-1, \\
C_i(x_{i+1}) &= y_{i+1}, && i = 0,\dots,n-1, \\
\dot{C}_i(x_{i+1}) &= \dot{C}_{i+1}(x_{i+1}), && i = 0,\dots,n-2, \\
\ddot{C}_i(x_{i+1}) &= \ddot{C}_{i+1}(x_{i+1}), && i = 0,\dots,n-2.
\end{aligned} \tag{1}
$$

The $n$ cubics carry $4n$ coefficients, while (1) supplies $2n + 2(n-1) = 4n-2$ conditions: two further conditions, one at each end, are needed ([[#Boundary conditions|boundary conditions]]).

== Derivation ==

Write $h_i = x_{i+1}-x_i$ and $f_i = y_{i+1}-y_i$. Differentiating the cubic once and twice,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{C}_i(x) &= 3a_i(x-x_i)^2 + 2b_i(x-x_i) + c_i, \\
\ddot{C}_i(x) &= 6a_i(x-x_i) + 2b_i.
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
$$

'''The constants $d_i$.''' At the left end of piece $i$ only $d_i$ survives, so the interpolation condition gives

$$
C_i(x_i) = d_i = y_i. \tag{3}
$$

'''Three equations for the remaining coefficients.''' At the right end of piece $i$, continuity of value, of slope and of curvature gives

$$
a_i h_i^3 + b_i h_i^2 + c_i h_i = f_i, \tag{4}
$$

$$
3a_i h_i^2 + 2b_i h_i + c_i = c_{i+1}, \tag{5}
$$

$$
6a_i h_i + 2b_i = 2b_{i+1} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad 3a_i h_i + b_i = b_{i+1}. \tag{6}
$$

Equation (6) links $b_i$ to $b_{i+1}$ for $i = 0,\dots,n-2$. Extended to $i = n-1$ it defines one more value of the same kind,

$$
b_n = 3a_{n-1}h_{n-1} + b_{n-1},
$$

which leaves $b_0,\dots,b_n$ as the unknowns and $a_i$, $c_i$ as functions of them.

'''Eliminate $a_i$.''' Dividing (6) by $3h_i$,

$$
a_i = \frac{b_{i+1}-b_i}{3h_i}, \qquad i = 0,\dots,n-1. \tag{7}
$$

'''Eliminate $c_i$.''' Solving (4) for $c_i$ and inserting (7),

$$
\begin{aligned}
c_i &= \frac{f_i - a_i h_i^3 - b_i h_i^2}{h_i} \\
&= \frac{f_i}{h_i} - \frac{1}{h_i}\left(\frac{b_{i+1}-b_i}{3h_i}\,h_i^3 + b_i h_i^2\right) \\
&= \frac{f_i}{h_i} - \frac{h_i}{3}\left(b_{i+1} + 2b_i\right), \qquad i = 0,\dots,n-1.
\end{aligned} \tag{8}
$$

'''One equation per interior knot.''' Inserting (7) and (8) into (5),

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{b_{i+1}-b_i}{h_i}\,h_i^2 + 2b_i h_i + \frac{f_i}{h_i} - \frac{h_i}{3}\left(b_{i+1}+2b_i\right)
&= \frac{f_{i+1}}{h_{i+1}} - \frac{h_{i+1}}{3}\left(b_{i+2}+2b_{i+1}\right), \\
\frac{h_i}{3}b_i + \frac{2h_i}{3}b_{i+1} + \frac{f_i}{h_i}
&= \frac{f_{i+1}}{h_{i+1}} - \frac{2h_{i+1}}{3}b_{i+1} - \frac{h_{i+1}}{3}b_{i+2}, \\
\frac{h_i}{3}b_i + \frac{2}{3}\left(h_i+h_{i+1}\right)b_{i+1} + \frac{h_{i+1}}{3}b_{i+2}
&= \frac{f_{i+1}}{h_{i+1}} - \frac{f_i}{h_i},
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
$$

for $i = 0,\dots,n-2$: that is $n-1$ equations for the $n+1$ unknowns $b_0,\dots,b_n$.<ref>{{#cite:Q2381}}</ref>

=== Boundary conditions ===

The two missing conditions sit one at each end.

'''Natural.''' The curvature vanishes at both ends, $\ddot{C}(x_0) = \ddot{C}(x_n) = 0$. Since $\ddot{C}_i(x_i) = 2b_i$ by (2),

$$
b_0, b_n = 0. \tag{10}
$$

'''Not-a-knot.''' The first two pieces and the last two pieces are each a single cubic, so the third derivative stays continuous at $x_1$ and at $x_{n-1}$ and those two nodes cease to be knots. On piece $i$ the third derivative is the constant $6a_i$, hence

$$
a_0 = a_1, \qquad a_{n-2} = a_{n-1}.
$$

Through (7),

$$
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{b_1-b_0}{3h_0} = \dfrac{b_2-b_1}{3h_1} \\[3mm]
\dfrac{b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}}{3h_{n-2}} = \dfrac{b_n-b_{n-1}}{3h_{n-1}},
\end{cases}
$$

and multiplying the first line by $3h_0h_1$ and the second by $3h_{n-2}h_{n-1}$,

$$
\begin{cases}
h_1 b_0 - (h_0+h_1)b_1 + h_0 b_2 = 0, \\[2mm]
h_{n-1}b_{n-2} - (h_{n-2}+h_{n-1})b_{n-1} + h_{n-2}b_n = 0.
\end{cases} \tag{11}
$$

'''Clamped.''' Both end slopes are prescribed, $\dot{C}(x_0) = \alpha$ and $\dot{C}(x_n) = \beta$. At the left end $\dot{C}_0(x_0) = c_0$, so by (8)

$$
\frac{2}{3}h_0 b_0 + \frac{1}{3}h_0 b_1 = \frac{f_0}{h_0} - \alpha .
$$

At the right end $\dot{C}_{n-1}(x_n) = 3a_{n-1}h_{n-1}^2 + 2b_{n-1}h_{n-1} + c_{n-1}$, which by (7) and (8) reduces to

$$
\dot{C}_{n-1}(x_n) = \frac{h_{n-1}}{3}b_{n-1} + \frac{2h_{n-1}}{3}b_n + \frac{f_{n-1}}{h_{n-1}} = \beta .
$$

Together,

$$
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2}{3}h_0 b_0 + \dfrac{1}{3}h_0 b_1 = \dfrac{f_0}{h_0} - \alpha, \\[3mm]
\dfrac{1}{3}h_{n-1}b_{n-1} + \dfrac{2}{3}h_{n-1}b_n = \beta - \dfrac{f_{n-1}}{h_{n-1}}.
\end{cases} \tag{12}
$$

The natural condition suits data whose curvature vanishes at the ends; the clamped condition suits data whose end slopes are known from outside the data; the not-a-knot condition assumes nothing about the ends and is the usual default.

== Linear system ==

Rows $2$ to $n$ of the system come from (9), and the first and last rows from the chosen pair of end conditions. For the not-a-knot pair (11),

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
h_1 & -(h_0+h_1) & h_0 & 0 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\[1mm]
\dfrac{1}{3}h_0 & \dfrac{2}{3}(h_0+h_1) & \dfrac{1}{3}h_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0 & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & & & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots & \dfrac{1}{3}h_{n-2} & \dfrac{2}{3}(h_{n-2}+h_{n-1}) & \dfrac{1}{3}h_{n-1} \\[2mm]
0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots & h_{n-1} & -(h_{n-2}+h_{n-1}) & h_{n-2}
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} b_0 \\ b_1 \\ \vdots \\ b_{n-1} \\ b_n \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\[1mm] \dfrac{f_1}{h_1} - \dfrac{f_0}{h_0} \\ \vdots \\ \dfrac{f_{n-1}}{h_{n-1}} - \dfrac{f_{n-2}}{h_{n-2}} \\[2mm] 0 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

The natural conditions put a $1$ on the diagonal of the first and last rows and a $0$ in the last two entries of the right-hand side; (12) supplies those two rows when the end slopes are prescribed. Each row touches at most three consecutive columns, so the matrix is tridiagonal and the system costs $O(n)$ operations instead of the $O(n^3)$ of a dense solver. From (2) at $x = x_i$, the unknown $b_i = \ddot{C}_i(x_i)/2$ is half the second derivative at knot $i$, and (3), (7) and (8) then give $d_i$, $a_i$ and $c_i$.<ref>{{#cite:Q2381}}</ref>

== Python implementation ==

<syntaxhighlight lang="python" copy>
import numpy as np

def cubic_spline(x, y, bc="not-a-knot"):
    """Coefficients of the cubic spline interpolating (x[i], y[i]).

    bc is "not-a-knot", "natural", or a pair (alpha, beta) of end slopes.
    Piece i is a[i]*(t-x[i])**3 + b[i]*(t-x[i])**2 + c[i]*(t-x[i]) + d[i].
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = len(x) - 1
    if n < 3:
        raise ValueError("at least 4 data points are required")

    h = np.diff(x)
    f = np.diff(y)

    A = np.zeros((n + 1, n + 1))        # one row per equation, one column per b[i]
    r = np.zeros(n + 1)

    for i in range(n - 1):              # eq. (9), rows 2 to n
        A[i + 1, i]     = h[i] / 3
        A[i + 1, i + 1] = 2 * (h[i] + h[i + 1]) / 3
        A[i + 1, i + 2] = h[i + 1] / 3
        r[i + 1] = f[i + 1] / h[i + 1] - f[i] / h[i]

    if bc == "natural":                 # eq. (10)
        A[0, 0] = A[n, n] = 1.0
    elif bc == "not-a-knot":            # eq. (11)
        A[0, 0], A[0, 1], A[0, 2] = h[1], -(h[0] + h[1]), h[0]
        A[n, n - 2], A[n, n - 1], A[n, n] = h[n - 1], -(h[n - 2] + h[n - 1]), h[n - 2]
    else:                               # eq. (12), clamped
        alpha, beta = bc
        A[0, 0], A[0, 1] = 2 * h[0] / 3, h[0] / 3
        r[0] = f[0] / h[0] - alpha
        A[n, n - 1], A[n, n] = h[n - 1] / 3, 2 * h[n - 1] / 3
        r[n] = beta - f[n - 1] / h[n - 1]

    b = np.linalg.solve(A, r)
    a = (b[1:] - b[:-1]) / (3 * h)                  # eq. (7)
    c = f / h - h * (2 * b[:-1] + b[1:]) / 3        # eq. (8)
    d = y[:-1]                                      # eq. (3)
    return x, a, b[:-1], c, d


def spline_eval(spline, t, deriv=0):
    """Value of the spline, or of its first three derivatives, at t."""
    x, a, b, c, d = spline
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    i = np.clip(np.searchsorted(x, t, side="right") - 1, 0, len(a) - 1)
    dx = t - x[i]
    if deriv == 0:
        return a[i] * dx**3 + b[i] * dx**2 + c[i] * dx + d[i]
    if deriv == 1:
        return 3 * a[i] * dx**2 + 2 * b[i] * dx + c[i]
    if deriv == 2:
        return 6 * a[i] * dx + 2 * b[i]
    return 6 * a[i] * np.ones_like(dx)


def spline_integral(spline, lo, hi):
    """Exact integral of the spline from lo to hi."""
    x, a, b, c, d = spline
    edges = np.unique(np.concatenate(([lo, hi], x[(x > lo) & (x < hi)])))
    total = 0.0
    for u, v in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
        i = int(np.clip(np.searchsorted(x, 0.5 * (u + v), side="right") - 1, 0, len(a) - 1))
        s, w = u - x[i], v - u
        total += (a[i] * ((s + w)**4 - s**4) / 4 + b[i] * ((s + w)**3 - s**3) / 3
                  + c[i] * ((s + w)**2 - s**2) / 2 + d[i] * w)
    return total
</syntaxhighlight>

The comments give the equation that each line implements. `np.linalg.solve` is a dense solver, so a banded solver is preferable for a large number of knots.

`cubic_spline(x, y, bc)` returns the knots and the coefficient arrays $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$: `bc` takes `"natural"`, `"not-a-knot"`, or a pair `(alpha, beta)` of end slopes, and `spline_eval(spline, t, deriv)` evaluates the spline or one of its first three derivatives. `spline_integral(spline, lo, hi)` integrates it exactly, piece by piece.

== Worked example ==

{{Hidden example}}
'''Velocity of a rocket.''' The upward velocity of a rocket is tabulated at six times, spaced unevenly: $h_0 = 10\ \mathrm{s}$, $h_1, h_2 = 5\ \mathrm{s}$, $h_3 = 2.5\ \mathrm{s}$ and $h_4 = 7.5\ \mathrm{s}$.<ref>{{#cite:Q2382}}</ref>

{| class="wikitable"
! $t$ (s) !! $0$ !! $10$ !! $15$ !! $20$ !! $22.5$ !! $30$
|-
! $v$ (m/s) !! $0$ !! $227.04$ !! $362.78$ !! $517.35$ !! $602.97$ !! $901.67$
|}

The five cubics of the not-a-knot spline reproduce the tabulated velocities and give a continuous acceleration, so the spline can be differentiated and integrated:

$$
v(16) = 392.07\ \mathrm{m/s}, \qquad \dot{v}(16) = 29.67\ \mathrm{m/s^2},
$$

$$
\int_{11}^{16} v(t)\,dt = 1604.9\ \mathrm{m}.
$$

The natural spline through the same data gives $v(16) = 392.15\ \mathrm{m/s}$, $\dot{v}(16) = 29.75\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ and $1604.4\ \mathrm{m}$. Piecewise linear interpolation gives $v(16) = 393.7\ \mathrm{m/s}$ and the quadratic spline in the source gives $395.50\ \mathrm{m/s}$: the four methods agree to within $1\%$, but only the cubic splines have a continuous acceleration.

[[File:Rocket velocity cubic spline.png|thumb|none|560px|alt=Two stacked line charts: velocity against time with the measured points, the piecewise linear interpolant and two cubic splines; below them, the corresponding accelerations|Velocity against time, and the acceleration $\dot{v}$ obtained from the spline. The acceleration is continuous at every knot, that of the piecewise linear interpolant jumps.]]

<syntaxhighlight lang="python" copy>
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t_data = np.array([0.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 22.5, 30.0])
v_data = np.array([0.0, 227.04, 362.78, 517.35, 602.97, 901.67])

spline = cubic_spline(t_data, v_data, bc="not-a-knot")
natural = cubic_spline(t_data, v_data, bc="natural")

print(spline_eval(spline, 16.0))            # velocity at 16 s
print(spline_eval(spline, 16.0, deriv=1))   # acceleration at 16 s
print(spline_integral(spline, 11.0, 16.0))  # distance covered from 11 s to 16 s

fig, (top, bottom) = plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True,
                                  gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1.6, 1]})
t = np.linspace(t_data[0], t_data[-1], 500)

top.plot(t_data, v_data, "o", color="#c0392b", label="measured data")
top.plot(t, np.interp(t, t_data, v_data), "--", color="0.55", label="piecewise linear")
top.plot(t, spline_eval(natural, t), ":", color="#e67e22", label="natural cubic spline")
top.plot(t, spline_eval(spline, t), color="#1f4e79", label="not-a-knot cubic spline")
top.set_ylabel("velocity $v$ (m/s)")
top.legend(frameon=False)

bottom.plot(t, spline_eval(spline, t, deriv=1), color="#1f4e79", label="not-a-knot cubic spline")
bottom.step(t_data, np.append(np.diff(v_data) / np.diff(t_data), np.nan), where="post",
            color="0.55", label="piecewise linear")
bottom.set_xlabel("time $t$ (s)")
bottom.set_ylabel("acceleration $\\dot v$ (m/s$^2$)")
bottom.legend(frameon=False)

for ax in (top, bottom):
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
</syntaxhighlight>
